sections.title: Executive Verdict
sections.text: Moxsh is a medical-education counselling, exam-content and overseas skill-mobility services business, not an asset-light compounder demonstrated by audited cash returns. Its useful destination knowledge and education content are outweighed, for investment research, by the FY26 revenue-recognition and asset-support qualifications. Reported consolidated PAT of ₹2.3031 crore becomes a ₹1.3902 crore loss in the filed partial qualification adjustment, before three additional unquantified items. At ₹107.95, the ₹102.56 crore equity capitalization therefore cannot be justified using reported earnings alone. This is an unverified turnaround/special-situation thesis. Conclusion: Hold — unresolved; no ordinary return estimate, entry price or ranking eligibility. Auditor-supported corrections, collections and a funded balance-sheet plan would matter more than a cheaper quote.

sections.title: Research Header, Gates and Data Confidence
sections.text:
Identity is MOXSH OVERSEAS EDUCON LIMITED, NSE Emerge symbol MOXSH, ISIN INE0N6D01014, CIN L74994MH2018PLC308826. Incorporated in2018; earlier brand experience is not an equal-length listed financial history. Financial scope is consolidated parent plus100%-owned Meduclinic Healthcare Private Limited. Xera Global Education is a promoter-related customer outside consolidation. The financial policies use Indian Accounting Standards in the generic Indian-GAAP sense, specifically notified Accounting Standards, not an Ind-AS IFRS-style lease model. No fictitious lease debt is introduced.

Information cutoff20 October 2026; market reference19 October 2026; five-year ownership interval20 October 2026–20 October 2031, nominal pretax equity hurdle15%, with12% and18% tests. Price ₹107.95, current shares9,500,800, market cap ₹102.561136 crore. Reference execution position ₹500,000 is a research convention, not a personal allocation recommendation. Confidence is High in security identity and what the filings say, Medium in bounded historical diagnosis, Low in normalized FY26 earnings, incremental returns and current financeability. A primary audit is evidence of the qualification, not proof that its reported profit is reliable. Gates G1 Conditional, G2 Hold, G3 Hold, G4 Conditional are detailed below.

sections.title: Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text:
All13 canonical factors are assessed once and reused under the actual v3.0 weights. GOV 4, MOAT3, DUR4, CASH 2, EXEC3 and downsideD2 are bounded judgments; REV,CAP,BAL,EARN,R,P,L remain NS. BQS has68% weighted coverage, known contribution2.24 and mathematical missing-data bound2.56–5.44; there is no midpoint score. GQS has30% coverage and known contribution1.00, with raw bound1.70–8.00. Persistent CASH 2 imposes the framework ceiling5, so its capped bound is1.70–5.00 while its point remains NS. IAS uses BQS once throughQ, not GQS; with onlyD2 scoreable it has20% coverage, known contribution0.40 and bound1.20–8.40. These are mathematical bounds, not confidence intervals or price forecasts.

GOV 4 does not activate the severe-governance override. Material G2 independently excludes all three rankings. Missing factors are not replaced by5 or reweighted. Lowering/raising MOAT byone changes the BQS known contribution by0.20; CASH byone changes BQS/GQS known contributions by0.10 each, without curing missingness. Only if new substantiated evidence justified GOV 3 would the governance override become relevant; that is not the current verdict.

sections.title: Business Overview
sections.text:
The core service connects Indian students with overseas medical education, guides admissions and supports medical licensing preparation. Counselling is economically a conversion business: inquiries must become paying enrolled students, universities or channel customers must pay agreed fees, and refunds and delivery obligations must be honored. Online exam-content development and licensing can create repeat usage, but require content refresh, faculty and selling expenditure. Subsidiary Meduclinic adds Germany-oriented skill-mobility programs and proposed digital classrooms/clinics. No audited segment profitability or clean customer-cohort cash economics is available.

FY26 revenue categories are professional fees ₹9.9929 crore, other services ₹0.7441 crore, software licences ₹1.77 crore and content development ₹0.40 crore. Those labels do not establish an independent SaaS recurring-revenue franchise. Related-party Xera fees of ₹4.3499 crore are inside, not additional to, the reported revenue total. The ₹0.97 crore unbilled item may overlap software; it must not be added or subtracted twice in a mix bridge. Recognition, cash collection and tuition/student throughput are different quantities. The latest annual report acknowledges contraction in overseas MBBS admissions, making the new channels important but unproved.

sections.title: Moat / Industry Position
sections.text:
A genuine edge could come from trusted university relationships, regulatory navigation, student referrals, reusable medical content and lower acquisition cost per paying student. The record does not establish pricing power, defensible exclusivity across destinations, long-lived customer retention or superior cash returns on content. University and migration rules can change; geopolitics and domestic medical-seat availability alter demand. Management claims about recognition in specific countries and exclusive university arrangements are treated as management assertions, not independent regulatory verification. No admission or medical-licensure eligibility advice is given.

Three economic comparators bound the story. IDP combines international student placement with IELTS co-ownership, which gives testing economics not demonstrated at Moxsh. CL Educate combines test preparation with assessment and marketing operations; its business mix and scale do not justify transferring a group multiple. Global Education supplies institutional consultancy, training, placement and IT services, rather than a like-for-like outbound-medical recruitment portfolio. These comparisons support contestability and the need for customer-level proof, not a top-three market-share claim. Current comparable-market multiples were not verified and are intentionally omitted.

sections.title: Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text:
Five audited consolidated years show revenue ₹10.0830,12.4303,10.6382,9.6559 and12.9070 crore for FY22–FY26. Absolute annual additions, margins and CAGR endpoints are embedded below. The three-year FY23–FY26 reported CAGR is only1.26%, versus a two-year FY23–FY25 decline of11.86% annually. FY26 reported growth is33.67%, but the increase includes disputed related-party course timing and new licensing/content categories. The partially adjusted total-income figure ₹8.7397 crore must not be mislabeled revenue; its implied operations component is ₹8.5532 crore after removing the unchanged ₹0.1865 crore other income.

FY20 and FY21 standalone restated revenues ₹8.1404 and ₹3.8631 crore provide pandemic-era context, not a manufactured comparable five-year group CAGR. FY26 H1 revenue ₹2.4083 crore and loss ₹2.3942 crore contrast with balancingH2 revenue ₹10.4987 crore and profit ₹4.6972 crore. H2 is full-year audited less unauditedH1, not a separately audited quarterly run rate. No H1FY27 result was located by cutoff, and later results are not backfilled. No acquisition, price, student-count or organic-growth bridge is invented where the issuer does not disclose it.

sections.title: Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text:
Bottom-up growth would require more paying students or paid licence users, stable realized fees, lower acquisition cost, timely university/channel collections and content investment that earns repeat cash contribution. Management's114 India-counselling students at average ₹18,000 imply ₹20.52 lakh of nominal first-year billings if the figures describe the same paid cohort; this is only a scale check, not a replacement audited revenue number. The claims of25,000 inquiries and1,200+Xera agents do not disclose active productivity, cancellations, fees received or cohort lifetime value. A large market estimate is not accessible revenue.

Reinvestment has not been free. FY26 gross PPE/intangible additions ₹8.1834 crore include old construction and advances, while fresh capital advances for content reached ₹1.9840 crore. The historical Studium expansion failed to materialize as planned because of regulatory/geographic problems. Reclassifying its prior capital is not proof of a successful new cohort. New FOCO classroom/clinic and migration projects require permits, operators, student demand and cash discipline. Because earnings, capitalization and cash recovery remain disputed, CAP and EARN cannot be scored, and persistent CASH 2 caps even the incomplete growth-quality bound at5. No management capacity/TAM claim is converted mechanically into the model's revenue.

sections.title: Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text:
The central issue is minority-shareholder confidence in accruals and capital allocation, not an unsupported accusation of fraud. FY26 statutory audit challenges Xera service timing, the absence of supplied Board approval/arm's-length support, capitalization documentation, software cutoff/valuation and aged receivables. Management disagrees, citing service obligations, invoices, approvals and recoverability. Secretarial audit independently reports inadequate support for ordinary-course/arm's-length exemptions. AOC2 cites a prior Board approval, while CARO says related-party compliance is satisfactory. These conflicting statements are retained, rather than selectively choosing the most favorable or adverse sentence.

Full audit annexures matter: FY23 main/IFC qualification concerned unconfirmed current-asset debit balances; FY24 opinions were unmodified; FY25 contained an aged-receivable emphasis and bank-return differences; FY26 introduces the four quantified/unquantified matters. Positive evidence includes no detected fraud, no recorded default, no reported material long-overdue statutory dues, appropriate stated issue use, unmodified current IFC and operational audit trail. These observations do not eliminate the qualifications. September2026 auditor resignation cites professional commitments and no other material reason. It happened after FY26, so 'no resignation during the year' is not contradictory. Successor appointment business was presented at the AGM; no inference that a replacement auditor already validated disputed FY26 amounts.

Capital raises reconcile: FY26 received ₹3.3408 crore, not the full ₹4.3008 crore potential preferential amount. Stated use ₹2.6398 crore leaves ₹0.7010 crore of actual received cash before other movements, not ₹1.6610 crore. The remaining ₹0.96 crore arrived in three dated post-year-end conversions. This amount is counted once. Bonus shares are not fresh cash; the377,600 new shares and160,000 warrant shares expand the post-bonus base by6%. All warrants had converted byJuly; no optional future warrant proceeds remain.

sections.title: Financial Forensics
sections.text:
The embedded historical statements, balance bridges and ratios are reported diagnostics, not normalized economics. FY23–FY25 cumulative CFO is−₹8.8374 crore against cumulative PAT−₹1.8323 crore, so the conversion ratio isNM, not a positive success ratio from two negatives. FY22–FY26 cumulative CFO−₹3.3201 crore divided by PAT ₹1.5620 crore equals−2.1255x, but the qualified FY26 numerator/denominator make this diagnostic only. Capex is below CFO: it cannot explain away poor operating cash conversion. FY26 CFO ₹4.9830 crore contains ₹2.8087 crore growth in payables while receivables absorb ₹1.2524 crore. Reported capex ₹6.5301 crore leaves FCF−₹1.5471 crore before ₹0.6184 crore financing interest.

Gross asset additions are not all fresh cash: oldCWIP ₹1.6497 crore and capital advances ₹1.2150 crore transfer to PPE. A classification bridge removes the old noncash advance transfer and includes fresh content advances, giving analytical CFO ₹5.7520 crore and economic reinvestment ₹7.2991 crore, still FCF−₹1.5471 crore. This is a cash-classification explanation, not an alleged total-cash misstatement. The ₹1.2150 crore FY24 transfer from the failed subsidiary expansion was likewise not new FY24 cash use. Trade creditors, capital creditors and total commitments are not fully broken into signed future purchase schedules; the model explicitly runs down legacy liabilities and adds new maintenance/content capex rather than double counting the full gross additions.

Invested capital is shown as reported owners' funds plus warrant deposits plus gross debt less cash equivalents. Restricted deposits remain deployed capital; no unsupported lease liability is invented. NOPAT uses operating EBIT excluding other income at25% tax. Both average and incremental ratios are disclosed, but large qualified revenue, receivables, intangibles, capitalization transfers and occasional negative capital deltas prevent a reliable CAP score. Reported EPS denominators are affected by bonuses/weighted shares and inconsistent comparatives; economic PAT per current9.5008 million shares is separately shown, never presented as statutory EPS.

March2026 receivables ₹9.5627 crore include Xera ₹5.0459 crore and ₹1.6848 crore over two years. Othercurrentassets include ₹0.97 crore disputed unbilled revenue. Cash equivalents are only ₹0.0434 crore;₹0.7031 crore fixed deposits are not assumed unrestricted. Debt ₹3.5713 crore includes ₹1.6128 crore secured bank OD and ₹1.9585 crore promoter demand funding. The debtor-age, related-party and bank-statement confirmations needed for a dependable current liquidity map remain unresolved. Meduclinic's negative net worth and related revenue qualification reinforce rather than diversify the accounting exposure; its parent loan is eliminated on consolidation. The component audit separately notes accumulated losses of ₹27.33405 lakh, eroded net worth and management confidence in raising director/shareholder finance to meet obligations. CARO nevertheless says no one-year material uncertainty. Preserve both statements: the prospective support is not independently committed group liquidity.

sections.title: Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text:
At ₹107.95 and9,500,800 shares, market cap is ₹102.561136 crore. The reported PAT multiple is44.53x using current shares, and the reported book multiple is about6.74x including the warrant deposit in FY26 net worth; current warrant conversion does not create fresh earnings. These are unsafe accounting cross-checks, not justified targets. The filed partial adjustment produces a loss, making normalizedP/E unavailable. EV uses gross debt less only verified cash equivalents, retaining restricted deposits; no liquid investment recovery or intangible appraisal is assumed. FY26 historical free-cash-flow yield is negative.

A reproducible cash model starts31 March 2026, not the investment date with imagined cash. It models operations to20 October 2026, then five exact anniversary years. The diagnostic revenue anchor ₹7.5832 crore removes the auditor's ₹4.3538 crore revenue impact and additionally excludes ₹0.97 crore disputed unbilled revenue. This conservative scenario anchor is not an auditor-certified fully restated revenue number. Clean, related, old and unbilled legacy claims collect at explicit scenario fractions/durations; old liabilities run off separately. New revenue invoices collect after60/90/180 days, costs and content capex consume cash, demand debt follows explicit rollover assumptions, and no bank headroom is invented. Tax is25% of positive EBIT with no interest-tax-shield or loss-carryforward benefit, a conservative simplification. Dividends are zero.

Bear/base/bull growth−5%/8%/18%, EBITDA margins4%/15%/24%, cash capex10%/8%/7% of sales and terminal EBITDA multiples4x/8x/12x are analyst stress assumptions, not guidance or peer-derived fair multiples. The required cash floor starts ₹0.15 crore and scales with revenue. Opening cash is already below this chosen reserve, but zero-reserve sensitivity separately tests operational deficits. None of the original paths is independently financeable; all ordinary and conditional non-rescue IRR/entry fields stay NS. Endpoint prices are merely signed-cash arithmetic, not targets.

An explicit hypothetical rescue pre-funds the maximum gap from31 March, assumes a30% discount to the October price and5% issuefees, rounds whole shares, and reruns the full path including pre-entry deficits. This is deliberately counterfactual, requires legal pricing, authorized capital, investor commitments and approvals, and is not available financing. Its diluted arithmetic and12%/15%/18% diagnostic discounted values must not be mistaken for investable entry ranges. The reverse-expectation scan has no verified funded crossing and reports no growth solution or endpoint fallback.

sections.title: Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text:
The strongest bear case is not simply that the market multiple falls. Related-party revenue reverses or is delayed, legacy dues do not convert into cash, capitalized content/furniture requires impairment, and current spending continues while bank or promoter demand funding is not renewed. Trade-creditor unwinding can reverse the reported cash improvement. A dilutive rescue would protect operations only by transferring a larger share of future value to new investors, and may not be legally or commercially available. Losses and intangible impairments can erode book value far faster than an apparently low debt/equity ratio suggests.

The linked bear case stresses receipts, margin, capex and debt rollover together. Separate grids isolate collection lag versus related recoveries and capex versus rollover; a deposit-release sensitivity shows why an unknown restriction cannot simply be netted away. Positive counterevidence is that published audits do not report a payment default and the company did receive ₹0.96 crore equity cash afteryear-end. Consequently the gate is a funding Hold, not a factual declaration of insolvency. Thesis-break evidence would be confirmed unrecoverable material dues or misappropriation, an actual unpaid essential obligation without committed support, or an auditor-backed finding that reported assets cannot sustain the operation. Merely observing an analyst reserve shortfall does not prove any such event.

sections.title: 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text:
A five- or tenfold share-price outcome would require far more than restoring reported FY26 profit. At the current share count and a diagnostic15% EBITDA margin and8x terminal multiple, required revenue must support the enlarged target equity value plus debt; those scale demands are shown below. Growth rates use the actualMarch2026 revenue-anchor-toOctober2031 duration, not a mismatched five-year denominator. Any rescue dilution or additional liabilities raises the required operating result.

This arithmetic is not a funded feasibility solution. No verified cohort productivity, pricing, retained customers, collection pattern or committed capital demonstrates the necessary scale. Large medical/migration TAM claims and capitalized software balances cannot substitute for those drivers. Classification: Speculative / unsupported, not an evidence-backed5× or10× candidate. Even the normal15% ownership hurdle has no supported funded reverse solution while G2/G3 remain open.

sections.title: Monitoring Plan
sections.text:
Monitor the nine specific baselines below after each result or material exchange filing. Priority is auditor-supported resolution, not quarterly promotional news: quantify all four qualifications, reconcile Xera revenue/receivables to subsequent collections, establish cash/deposit restrictions and written demand-debt terms, and prove content-project returns. A change from NS to scoreable requires new evidence, not passage of time.

Use reported ₹1.6848 crore olddues and ₹5.0459 crore Xera dues as separate monitored disclosures; confirm their overlap or non-overlap before relying on model recovery buckets. Track fresh capital advances ₹1.9840 crore, subsequent capitalization, actual paid customers and realized fees. Bank-return differences must be rectified rather than merely explained. Liquidity monitoring must fill the absent-row classification and assess live spread/depth at whole-lot size. These are research review triggers, not an automated alert subscription or trading instruction.

sections.title: Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text:
Final classification is Hold — unresolved, with research priority focused on reliability and funding. It is not an evidence-backed compounder candidate and is ineligible for all BQS/GQS/IAS rankings. A lower price alone does not cure unquantified asset/revenue adjustments or make an unverified funding plan executable. Conversely, a qualified opinion and thin cash do not prove fraud, zero recovery or imminent default. The evidence supports a disciplined unresolved classification rather than a confident buy or an allegation.

For an existing holding, this would be a review candidate on accounting, funding, valuation and execution grounds, not an automatic sale instruction; actual holdings, tax basis and portfolio constraints were not supplied. A ₹500,000 reference position is2lots costing ₹345,440 or3lots costing ₹518,160, making even sizing coarse. Actual exit time and slippage are unknown. Resolution requires corrected accounts, confirmed collections and debt capacity, and tradability evidence before a return-based entry decision can be assessed.

sections.title: Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
sections.text:
The source ledger retains direct primary URLs, exact file hashes where downloaded, retrieval dates and claim locators. Full FY26 parent/consolidated audit, CARO, IFC, secretarialreport, management responses, componentaudit and prior-year qualification history were read; favorable and adverse findings are both preserved. NSE master and all60 actual ZIP archives were validated by payload hashes, ZIPintegrity and embedded trade/business dates. Original filings, shareholder lists, OCR, images, personal identifiers and transfer helpers are excluded from distributable source-safe archives. Reproduction verifies arithmetic and hashes, not the truth of issuer disclosures.

Open material questions are the timing and eventual collections for Xera courses; exact support/impairment for ₹2.8647 crore PPE, software and content; recoverability/overlap of aged claims; Board and shareholder approval basis; residual difference in reported versus auditor RPT amounts; restricted deposit availability; current bank/promoter terms and cash; and verified no-trade status for missing market rows. Normalized PAT, reliable incrementalROIC, ordinaryIRR, entryprice, full-window liquidity and affected factors remain NS. The FY26 annual report says no credit rating was obtained during the year. Searches of major rating-agency sources did not establish a later current rating; absence of a rating is not a default finding. Source discrepancies of ₹0.39 lakh RPT revenue and ₹0.01 lakh related dues, the ₹0.02 lakh FY24 PAT comparative difference, and cash-flow rounding are disclosed, not silently repaired.

No publication, Gitpush, investment transaction or external outreach is part of this company package. Figures are analytical research, and no assumption is represented as a verified company commitment.

evidence.fact: Moxsh Overseas Educon Limited is MOXSH, ISIN INE0N6D01014, CIN L74994MH2018PLC308826. Consolidation includes the wholly owned Meduclinic subsidiary; Xera is an external related party.

FY26 consolidated revenue is ₹12.9070 crore and PAT ₹2.3031 crore, with a qualified opinion. The filed partial adjustment reduces total income to ₹8.7397 crore and PAT to a ₹1.3902 crore loss; three other impacts remain unquantified.

Other FY26 qualifications concern ₹286.47 lakh PPE capitalization without adequate architect/location cost support, ₹97 lakh unbilled software valuation and cutoff, and ₹168.48 lakh receivables over two years without provision.

Management says contractual services were completed, related transactions were approved and at arm’s length, PPE invoices supported capitalization, software was ready in March, and old dues remained recoverable. No auditor-agreed resolution was located.

Secretarial audit says ordinary-course and arm’s-length support was insufficient, with shareholder approval absent if exemptions did not apply. AOC2 cites February 2025 Board approval, while statutory audit says approval was not supplied. CARO asserts compliance. The conflict is unresolved.

FY26 bank-return differences, books minus submitted figures, are −₹15.24 lakh, −₹55.29 lakh and −₹43.79 lakh for June, September and December; not rectified. The CC closed in February. Favorable findings include no detected fraud/default, no material statutory dues older than six months, appropriate issue use, an unmodified IFC opinion and functioning audit trail.

FY23 main audit and IFC opinions were qualified for missing current-asset confirmations/reconciliations. FY24 opinions were unmodified. FY25 was unmodified with a ₹358.66 lakh aged-receivable emphasis and unrectified bank-return differences. A later clean IFC does not erase this history.

Old CWIP ₹1.6497 crore and advances ₹1.2150 crore transferred into PPE, not fresh cash. Gross additions ₹8.1834 crore reconcile to reported capex after CWIP and an inferred ₹0.36 lakh residual. Reclassifying advance cash yields analytical CFO ₹5.7520 crore and reinvestment ₹7.2991 crore, preserving FCF −₹1.5471 crore.

March 2026 debt comprises bank OD ₹1.6128 crore at 9.5% and promoter demand funding ₹1.9585 crore at 12%. Deposits ₹0.7031 crore are not assumed free cash. Current sanction headroom, cash and rollover terms are unverified; recoverability and reinvestment obligations compound thin cash.

FY26 equity/warrant receipts were ₹334.08 lakh, not the ₹430.08 lakh full potential amount. Use ₹263.98 lakh leaves ₹70.10 lakh of received proceeds, not ₹166.10 lakh. Later receipts on 12 May, 6 June and 9 July total ₹96 lakh; all warrants converted.

Shares reconcile from 8,963,200 after the bonus to 9,340,800 after January equity, then 9,500,800 after warrant conversions. Face value ₹10 and lot 1,600 are verified. The stale SQ master row is not the active SM denominator.

March receivables ₹9.5627 crore include Xera ₹5.0459 crore and old dues ₹1.6848 crore. The prior-year Xera receivable is blank and FY26 bookings support a current classification; model recovery buckets still require confirmation. Other current assets include ₹0.97 crore unbilled income.

Meduclinic reports revenue ₹1.3793 crore, PAT ₹0.1459 crore and negative net worth ₹0.2633 crore. Its audit qualifies Xera income ₹102.95 lakh and related receivables ₹119.42 lakh. CARO reports prior-year cash loss ₹43.97691 lakh but no current cash loss, default or detected fraud; IFC reporting is not applicable. A going-concern paragraph notes accumulated losses ₹27.33405 lakh and reliance on prospective director/shareholder finance, while CARO reports no one-year material uncertainty. Neither is a group default finding.

The 19 October SM close is ₹107.95, with 14,400 shares, ₹15.024 lakh traded value and eight trades. Market capitalization is ₹102.561136 crore. Only 30 of 60 and 12 of 20 calendar sessions contain issuer rows; absent rows are not confirmed zero trading.

One 1,600-share lot costs ₹172,720. A ₹500,000 reference rounds down to 3,200 shares costing ₹345,440 or up to 4,800 costing ₹518,160. At 2%, 5% or 10% participation the latest session permits zero whole lots under the constraint.

summary: Moxsh is a medical-education counselling, exam-content and overseas skill-mobility services business, not an asset-light compounder demonstrated by audited cash returns. Its useful destination knowledge and education content are outweighed, for investment research, by the FY26 revenue-recognition and asset-support qualifications. Reported consolidated PAT of ₹2.3031 crore becomes a ₹1.3902 crore loss in the filed partial qualification adjustment, before three additional unquantified items. At ₹107.95, the ₹102.56 crore equity capitalization therefore cannot be justified using reported earnings alone. This is an unverified turnaround/special-situation thesis. Conclusion: Hold — unresolved; no ordinary return estimate, entry price or ranking eligibility. Auditor-supported corrections, collections and a funded balance-sheet plan would matter more than a cheaper quote.
